name: Glean
scope_notes: Glean-hosted enterprise SaaS (single tenant, <instance>-be.glean.com); plan tiers are not documented for these controls, and log delivery to customer storage needs Glean account team setup.

controls.name: Token scopes
controls.what: Token is limited to chosen Client API scopes, fixed at creation.

controls.name: Agent-scoped Client API token
controls.what: Token only works for the assigned agents and expires after one year.
controls.setting: API tokens page or agent Share > API

controls.name: Token creation roles
controls.what: Only admin roles or API Token Creator can create tokens; global scope needs Super Admin.

controls.name: Greenlisted IPs
controls.what: Per-token CIDR allowlist enforced on Indexing API requests.

controls.name: Expires On (required)
controls.what: Indexing tokens must have an expiry date.

controls.name: Rotation Period
controls.what: Token must be rotated via /rotatetoken within the set period (min 24h).

controls.name: Tenant-wide IP greenlist
controls.what: VPC firewall allowlist for the tenant; MCP also checks at app layer.

controls.name: Enable Glean OAuth Server
controls.what: Turns Glean-issued OAuth on or off.

controls.name: Dynamic client registration settings
controls.what: Allow any app, only approved apps/redirect URIs, or no DCR.
controls.setting: Settings > Third-party access (OAuth) > DCR > Manage settings

controls.name: Delete static client / Revoke client
controls.what: Ends access for all users of that client after config propagation.
controls.setting: Users & permissions > Third-party access (OAuth) > Delete client

controls.name: Rotate secret (static client)
controls.what: Old client secret stops working immediately.

controls.name: OAuth token TTL
controls.what: Admins can change access (7d) and refresh (180d) TTLs.

controls.name: Sign out of all sessions
controls.what: Invalidates a user's Glean-issued OAuth tokens (cache refresh ~10 min).

controls.name: Enable IDP OAuth for API access
controls.what: Turns on acceptance of IdP tokens for listed client IDs.

controls.name: Enterprise Managed Auth (trusted issuer, allowed scopes)
controls.what: EMA tokens limited to selected scopes; rejected without a trusted issuer.
controls.setting: Users & permissions > Third-party access (OAuth) > Enterprise Managed Auth

no_control.what: Token scopes and permission type cannot be edited after creation; must reissue.
OAuth/federated auth is not available for the Indexing API; only static Glean-issued tokens.

controls_unknown: Whether revoking a Glean-issued API token takes effect immediately
Whether user deprovisioning revokes that user's Glean-issued API tokens
Whether admin audit logs record API token create/revoke (coverage list does not mention tokens)
Per-token IP allowlist for Client API tokens
Default OAuth server state (admin docs: off; developer docs: on)
Where the tenant-wide IP greenlist is configured and whether customers manage it

authentication.summary: Glean-issued bearer token created in Admin console > Platform > API tokens, tied to one user and a fixed set of scopes (SEARCH, CHAT, DOCUMENTS, MCP, etc.). Can also be scoped to specific agents.

federation.details: Static token. Docs say it works without the identity provider, so it does not pass through SSO or IdP conditional access.

ip_restriction.boundary: Only the tenant-wide IP greenlist at the VPC firewall; no per-token IP list documented for Client API tokens.

lifetime.summary: Optional expiry date; agent-scoped tokens expire after 1 year

renewal.summary: Create a new token; scopes cannot be edited.

administration.summary: Admins and API Token Creators can make tokens for themselves; Super Admins for any user. Admins revoke from the API tokens page.
administration.conditions: No approval workflow or org-wide disable switch documented.

inventory.details: Admin console > Platform > API tokens lists Client API tokens.

network.ui: No self-serve setting; send Glean the allowed CIDRs and Glean enables IP green listing (tenant-wide)

expiry.ui: Admin console → Client API Token Settings → Add New Token → Expires (set at creation)

usage.ui: Query the glean-customer-event log (bucket/warehouse; ask account team for location); filter IsRestClientApi = true

reads.ui: In glean-customer-event log, filter jsonPayload.type = SEARCH and IsRestClientApi = true

token_format.notes: Only seen in an example header value; not a documented format.

log_sources.name: Glean Customer Event (GCE) logs
log_sources.notes: On by default; delivered to object storage/warehouse; customer export needs account team.

log_sources.name: Admin audit logs
log_sources.notes: Config changes only; 30-day default retention; CSV export.

credential_id_fields.notes: Flags API calls; no token ID field documented.

anomaly_cues: IsRestClientApi=true searches for a user who never used the API

containment.steps: Revoke the token in Admin console > Platform > API tokens.

authentication.summary: Glean-issued bearer token that can act as any user by sending X-Glean-ActAs: <email>.

federation.details: Static token; independent of the IdP.

administration.summary: Only Super Admins can create global tokens.
administration.conditions: Highest-impact Glean credential: impersonates any user.

offboard.details: GLOBAL tokens are not tied to one user; they can act as any user via X-Glean-ActAs.

network.ui: No self-serve setting; send Glean the allowed CIDRs and Glean enables IP green listing (tenant-wide)

expiry.ui: Admin console → Client API Token Settings → Add New Token → Expires (set at creation)

usage.ui: Query the glean-customer-event log (bucket/warehouse; ask account team for location); filter IsRestClientApi = true

reads.ui: In glean-customer-event log, filter jsonPayload.type = SEARCH and IsRestClientApi = true

log_sources.name: GCE logs
log_sources.notes: Events are attributed to the impersonated user.

anomaly_cues: API activity spread across many users at once (ActAs fan-out)

containment.steps: Revoke the global token in the API tokens page.

unknown: Whether logs record the ActAs caller vs. impersonated user

calls.reveals: Search results without permission checks (privileged users)

authentication.summary: Glean-issued bearer token for /api/index/v1 (push documents, permissions, datasources). Global or limited to selected datasources. OAuth is not accepted.

ip_restriction.boundary: Optional per-token Greenlisted IPs (CIDR); requests from other IPs get 403.

renewal.expiry_basis: fixed date; rotation does not extend it
renewal.summary: Optional rotation via /rotatetoken (min period 24h); old secret works 10 more minutes.

administration.summary: Setup Admins, Admins and Super Admins create tokens; only Super Admins grant global scope.
administration.conditions: Revoke from the API tokens page.

offboard.details: Indexing tokens give service-level access, not user access.

inventory.details: Admin console > Platform > API tokens (Indexing Tokens tab).

usage.ui: Admin console → Users & permissions → Audit logs; filter, Export to CSV (config changes only)

anomaly_cues: Unexpected permission or document updates in a datasource

containment.steps: Revoke the token in API tokens (Indexing tab).
containment.notes: After a rotation the old secret works for 10 more minutes.

credentials.name: Glean OAuth Authorization Server token (static and DCR clients, MCP)

authentication.summary: OAuth 2.1 authorization code + PKCE. User signs in through the tenant's SSO IdP; Glean issues a JWT access token with Glean scopes. Used by MCP hosts and Client/Platform API apps.

federation.details: User sign-in goes through the existing SSO IdP; tokens are then Glean-issued.

ip_restriction.boundary: Tenant VPC firewall greenlist; MCP endpoints enforce greenlisting at the app layer. OAuth metadata discovery may be exempt.

lifetime.summary: Access 7 days, refresh 180 days by default; admin-configurable

administration.summary: Admin toggle under Settings > Third-party access (OAuth). DCR defaults to allowing any application; admins can restrict to approved redirect URIs or block DCR. Static clients have admin-set scopes.
administration.conditions: Docs disagree on default: admin docs say off, developer docs say on.

sso.details: Users sign in through the org's existing SSO IdP before Glean issues the OAuth token.

inventory.details: Users see their own authorized applications. Admins manage clients in the Admin console but have no documented per-token list.

sso.ui: Admin console → Settings → Third‑party access (OAuth) → Enable Glean OAuth Server; sign-in uses the existing SSO IdP, so set MFA/conditional access in the IdP

network.ui: No self-serve setting; send Glean the allowed CIDRs and Glean enables IP green listing (tenant-wide)

usage.ui: MCP activity logs (filter by server, tool, user, date; shows OAuth client name); GCE log: type = MCP_USAGE, McpUsage.Application / AuthMethod

reads.ui: In glean-customer-event log, filter jsonPayload.type = MCP_USAGE (EventType TOOL_CALL, ToolName)

kill.ui: Users & permissions → Third‑party access (OAuth) → ⋮ next to client → Delete client; per user: User roles → ⋮ → Sign out of all sessions

token_format.notes: RS256 JWT with kid; verifiable via /api/oauth/jwks.

log_sources.name: Admin audit logs
log_sources.notes: Client create/revoke and OAuth setting changes.

anomaly_cues: New DCR client while DCR is set to Allow any application

containment.steps: Delete/revoke the client; sign the user out of all sessions.
containment.notes: Takes effect after ~5-10 min propagation / 10 min cache. Users can also revoke an app themselves, which deletes its consents and refresh tokens. Admins can list a static client's users via View users.

authentication.summary: Access tokens issued by the customer's IdP (Google, Entra ID, Okta, OneLogin) and sent with X-Glean-Auth-Type: OAUTH. Glean checks issuer and client_id.

federation.details: Admin registers issuer and allowed client IDs; IdP policy governs issuance.

ip_restriction.boundary: Tenant VPC firewall greenlist plus whatever the IdP enforces at issuance.

administration.summary: Off until an admin toggles Enable IDP OAuth for API access and lists allowed client IDs.

sso.details: The customer's IdP issues these tokens, so IdP assignments and policies decide whether a user gets one.

sso.ui: Register the OAuth app in the IdP and assign users/policies there; Admin console → Settings → Third‑party access (OAuth) → Enable IDP OAuth for API access → Manage Settings

network.ui: No self-serve setting; send Glean the allowed CIDRs and Glean enables IP green listing (tenant-wide)

expiry.ui: Set access/refresh token lifetime in the IdP's OAuth app policy (not in Glean)

usage.ui: Query the glean-customer-event log (bucket/warehouse; ask account team for location); filter IsRestClientApi = true

reads.ui: In glean-customer-event log, filter jsonPayload.type = SEARCH and IsRestClientApi = true

kill.ui: Revoke in the IdP; or Admin console → Settings → Third‑party access (OAuth) → Manage Settings → remove client ID from Allowed clientID(s), or toggle off Enable IDP OAuth for API access

anomaly_cues: Tokens from a client ID not on the allowed list (rejected)

containment.steps: Revoke in IdP; remove client ID or disable IdP OAuth in Glean.
containment.notes: Revocation follows the IdP's policies. Docs do not say whether Glean checks revocation for each request or accepts tokens until they expire.

credentials.name: Enterprise Managed Auth (JWT bearer assertion for MCP)

authentication.summary: An AI app sends an IdP-signed identity assertion to /oauth/token with the JWT bearer grant; Glean returns an MCP access token without a consent screen.

federation.details: Trusted issuer must be configured; currently Claude with Okta only.

renewal.summary: App obtains a new assertion from the IdP.

administration.summary: Off unless the EMA toggle is on and a trusted issuer is set; allowed scopes limit tokens.

sso.details: Each token comes from an IdP identity assertion, and admins control which users and apps can connect in the IdP.

offboard.details: No refresh tokens are issued, so once the IdP stops issuing assertions no new tokens are minted. Existing access tokens run until they expire.

sso.ui: In the IdP, register Glean as a Cross App Access resource server and assign users; in Glean: Users & permissions → Third-party access (OAuth) → Enterprise Managed Auth → Trusted issuer

network.ui: No self-serve setting; send Glean the allowed CIDRs and Glean enables IP green listing (tenant-wide)

usage.ui: MCP activity logs (filter by server, tool, user, date; shows OAuth client name); GCE log: type = MCP_USAGE, McpUsage.Application / AuthMethod

reads.ui: In glean-customer-event log, filter jsonPayload.type = MCP_USAGE (EventType TOOL_CALL, ToolName)

kill.ui: Users & permissions → Third-party access (OAuth) → turn off Enterprise Managed Auth, or delete the app's static client; then User roles → ⋮ → Sign out of all sessions to cut existing tokens

offboard.ui: Unassign the user in the IdP Cross App Access connection; Admin console → Users & permissions → User roles → ⋮ → Sign out of all sessions

containment.steps: Turn off EMA or remove the trusted issuer; unassign the user in the IdP.
containment.notes: Turning off EMA or removing the issuer leaves existing tokens valid until expiry. Admin 'sign out of all sessions' invalidates them after the revocation cache refreshes (~10 minutes).
